newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP sees US$1.00 copper price in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP sees US$1.00 copper price in 97/98.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) managing director John Prescott said on Monday pressure on copper prices had eased in recent weeks, but that BHP was still assuming a copper price of US$1.00 per pound over the next financial year to end-May 1998.
This compares with COMEX copper prices currently around A$1.19 per pound.

Prescott later said that BHP was focussed on restructuring the asset base at its copper operations and on cost-reduction of its copper production unit, and in particular Magma Copper in the United States.
He said BHP was targetting cost reductions across its copper division of about 10 U.S. cents per pound.
"We've got targets of about 10 cents a pound across the board," he said.
It was too early to say whether BHP would meet its targets but, "that hopefully will be bring the best out of us."
A reduction of 10 cents a pound would have a significant impact on BHP's bottom line, but would still leave Magma a higher cost operation than some of its competitors.
Copper companies typically guard production costs.
However, analyst estimate that rivals to BHP such as MIM Holdings Ltd maintain costs in the low to mid 70-cent range.
In parts of South America, costs can run as low as 30 or 40 cents a pound.
BHP in March said its North American copper costs were running at about 80 cents a pound. This compared with an average of 74 cents a pound prior to BHP buying Magma in 1995.
Copper on Friday closed at just over US$1.18 a pound.
Each one cent change in the copper price means A$16 million to BHP's bottom line, Prescott has said.
